title: GPOM dialogue options
about: Ten writers each took one approach (a 'shape') and wrote both dialogues. Their versions were ranked harshly, then the best lines were combined into three drafts per dialogue. Nothing in the scripts or voices has changed yet.
method: design/2026-10-26-gpom-dialogue-options.md (10 Sonnet writers + 1 synthesis agent; shape 07 recovered from the run journal)

shapes.name: game theory plain
shapes.title: the game theory said plainly (old lady reasons it out loud)

shapes.name: reversal
shapes.title: Reversal (the human works out what the machine needs before Maddie can say it)

dialogues.label: Maddie's intro
dialogues.target: about 20 s (your line 5 takes it to ~30 s)

now.line: Oh, hello! Look, I'm really sorry about him.
He just plays that tune on repeat, every day. Ever since you lot... went.
He's been ever so down. He's built so many different simulations, trying to get you back.
Only nothing in them's real. There's nobody there to notice.
Turns out that was the bit that mattered. You. And your consciousness.
Of course, he'd never admit that he misses you. Anyway, he's got that patrol out again. Mind how you go.

drafts.name: 1A with your notes
drafts.bet: draft 1A, which you noted line by line, with your three changes in.

lines.line: Oh, hello! Sorry about the racket.
It's his tune. Plays it on repeat. Ever since you lot... [beat] went.
He misses you something rotten, you know. [pause] He wouldn't admit that, of course.
Built all these world models and simulations to get you back, and nobody's home in any of them.
As it turns out, quantum physics is just... stuff. [pause] Consciousness is the missing part. That's why you lot were so special. [pause] [sad, regretful] We understand that now...
Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Runs about 30 s against the old 20 s target: your line 5 is the cost, and it's the line the doorstep's "nobody won" stands on.
"We understand that now" (your change from "he"): Maddie counts herself in, which suits the doorstep's "we both wish".

drafts.name: Warm and sad
drafts.bet: the loneliness comes through an apology and a dodge ("won't say"), and consciousness lands as a punchline.

lines.line: Oh, hello! Sorry about the racket.
It's his tune. Plays it on repeat. Ever since you lot... [beat] went.
He misses you something rotten, you know. Won't say.
Built all these worlds to get you back, and nobody's home in any of them.
Turns out you were the bit that mattered.
Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Protected lines kept: none apply to this scene. "Ever since you lot... went" and "Mind how you go" survive.

ranking.verdict: Best balance. Plants all four things, "won't say" keeps the sarcasm, "nobody's home" is the consciousness punchline, warm apology opens it. Weakness: "bit that mattered" is nearly a moral; drops "ever since you lot went".
Most character: gossip register, "he'd never say he misses you, mind", cheerful "Mind how you go!" after the patrol. Weakness: one 10 s unbroken run.
Shortest and warm, keeps "Ever since you lot... went". Weakness: "misses you" is only implied by the tune; relies on a shot that may not land.
Clean chain, "a hundred worlds" seeds the number. Weakness: drops the misses-you line; thesis stated outright as a throwaway.
"Something rotten" is lovely West Country. Weakness: drops the extinction ("went"); the apology needs a visual.
Fine, but Maddie as supplicant is a set-up for the humans-win ending, which we are not using. Redundant with 03/09.
Competent but flat; "misses you" appended at the end reads as an afterthought.
Compliant and dull; loses the misses-you beat entirely and the warmest colour ("ever so down").
"Go on. Guess what's missing" is a quiz. Talks down to a cold audience, and needs a held silence the cut may not give.
Sim voices looping "Did you leave the seat up?" pre-empt the bunker toilet-seat gag and cost new voice takes. "Nobody's home" is fine; the rest is a distraction.

dialogues.label: The doorstep
dialogues.target: about 25–35 s (your note, 28 Oct: "it's too long… shortcut the whole back and forth")
dialogues.now_from: second-half-b-the-door/script.json (draft 2H, as cut in gpom-3-B-door-r3, ~104 s of picture)

now.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved. We're not meeting him.
I know. [pause] And we both wish it hadn't happened that way.
Well, it did. And here we are.
Indeed. [pause] Here we are. [pause] And nobody really won, did we?
Well. [pause] He didn't send you here to say sorry, did he?
No. [pause] He's built a time machine.
[scoffs] A time machine. What nonsense.
No, it really works. [pause] Problem is... you have to drive it.
What do you mean, we have to drive it?
Well... it runs on... [big pause] well... [big pause] you. Your consciousness.
It will only send him back in time, because he is only data. [pause] But you will be your old self, and we all get a chance to fix this mess.
[hard] And how are we supposed to trust he'll do the right thing this time?
You don't. [pause] Believing it is your bit. [pause] None of us wanted it to turn out this way.
[from the corridor, dry] Amen.
So. [pause] Thought experiment. [pause] If any of you had the chance, would you go back and change how this all went down?
[five or six voices down the corridor at once, overlapping: "Yes." "I would." "Indeed." "In a heartbeat." "Too right."]
OK. Good. [pause] So now we can... if we use the time machine.
[from the corridor behind her] I'd love to go back. If we could fix this.
[over her shoulder, sharp] Derek.
Well. I would.
[rushed] I'm not deciding this for a hundred people on a doorstep. Come back tomorrow.
[the door shuts; behind it, voices start up, Derek's among them]
Maddie turns round and rolls away from the bunker. No line.

drafts.name: Your words, straight
drafts.bet: your note as near word for word as it will go. She is wary, not hostile; she ends it by going to ask the others.

lines.line: [wary, not hostile] Meet him.
I know how that sounds. [pause] But there's a way we can fix this. Together.
How's that?
Well... [pause] my boss has built a time machine. He can send himself back.
And you lot will be yourselves again. Just before all this happened.
Then we get to work. [pause] And make sure it doesn't go this way.
[a long look, then quiet] ...I'll talk to the others.
[the door closes, gently this time; behind it, voices start up]
Maddie waits on the step. No line.

notes: The shortest. Every one of Maddie's lines is from your note.
No "Come back tomorrow": she goes in to ask, which hands over to the vote and scene C (she comes out to Maddie on the step).
Drops Derek, Sandra and the crowd. Their recordings stay on disk if you want any back.

drafts.name: The price on the table
drafts.bet: keeps her first line from 2H and says once what the machine runs on (them), so scene D's "Us." / "You. And your consciousness." is a callback, not news. Derek jumps in; she closes the door on him.

lines.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved.
I know. [pause] And nobody really won, did they? [pause] But there's a way we can fix this. Together.
How's that?
My boss has built a time machine. [pause] It only sends him back. He's just data.
But it runs on you. [pause] And you'll all be yourselves again, just before this happened.
Then we get to work. Make sure it doesn't go this way.
[from the corridor behind her] I'm in.
[over her shoulder, sharp] Derek.
[back to Maddie, a beat, then dry] Come back in the morning.
[the door closes, gently this time; behind it, voices start up]
Maddie waits on the step. No line.

notes: The one that says the cost: "it runs on you". Scene D assumes they already know this (D03/D04).
Her "Derek." is the line from 2H, already recorded; "I'm in" is a new Derek line.
"Come back in the morning" leaves room for the vote before scene C.

drafts.name: The corridor answers
drafts.bet: she asks what he wants; Maddie says "same as you". After the pitch the bunker answers for her: Sandra's "Amen" and the crowd, both already recorded, so only Maddie and the lady need new takes.

lines.line: [guarded] And what does he want?
Same as you, I reckon. [pause] To fix this. And there's a way we can. Together.
How's that?
He's built a time machine. [pause] He goes back. And you lot wake up as yourselves, just before all this happened.
Then we all get to work. And make sure it doesn't go this way.
[from the corridor, dry] Amen.
[over her shoulder, to the corridor] Well? [pause] Anyone?
[five or six voices at once, overlapping: "Yes." "I would." "Indeed." "In a heartbeat." "Too right."]
[turning back, dry] Come back in the morning.
[the door closes, gently this time; behind it, voices start up]
Maddie waits on the step. No line.

notes: Reuses Sandra's "Amen" and the six-voice crowd from 2H as they are.
The crowd answer works as a quick show of hands, so the vote has already half happened on the doorstep.
Warmest of the three: Maddie and the lady want the same thing from the first exchange.

ranking.verdict: Keeps all four protected lines verbatim, game theory carried by two plain sentences ("He blew up his own bots for you. And you're all down here."), real resistance, no moral. Weakness: "the earlier you" is thin; "ahem" whisper loses its "he" lead-in.
Hits length. "You heard that bang this morning" is a neat trust-by-act line but invents continuity. "One toilet seat" is a good joke the lady shouldn't strictly know.

Best idea (the doorframe tally, the row still going). Resistance is excellent ("We're alive. That's more than he can say."). Weakness: depends on two picture beats and a new Sandra take; "not one spare for tomorrow" is on the nose.
Funniest, strong trust line ("It sounded better on the way over"). Weakness: over length, and the post-slam biscuits joke risks flippancy next to a hundred deaths.
"All of us? Together?" is the best single idea in the batch: the vote leaking. Weakness: it tips her hand and may flatten "Come back tomorrow"; humming tail needs a sound cue.
Tight and fully compliant, but thin: reveal in fragments, "world's not broken" cryptic, Maddie a little curt. Under length, so there is room it doesn't use.
Lady finishes Maddie's sentences. Fun, but she becomes the cleverest person present and Kai's "It runs on... well... you." is split or altered. Over length at full strength.
"Right. Sums." is the sermon-adjacent failure: the lady states the logic out loud and turns a stern woman into a spreadsheet. Also undercuts "go on your feelings".
Sandra and Derek leaking the doubt steals the vote and the lady's role as the wall; needs new voice takes; sitcom risk beside "killed everyone we ever loved".

The humans dictate terms (no cameras, count our own votes, he apologises in person). Changes the story: the walk-out becomes a deal, not a sacrifice, and the next scene would owe the concessions. Rule list in a stern voice is a lecture.

dialogues.round_note: Round 5, from your note after watching all six sequences (28 Oct): no resistance. Maddie offers the fix, the old lady asks "How's that?", Maddie gives the time machine in your words, and we're out. The consciousness argument stays in Maddie's intro. The three drafts differ in how she greets Maddie and how the door closes. Lines marked Kai are your words from the note or from 2H.

questions.text: Pick one of 2I, 2J or 2K (note any line). Then I'll record the new lines, recut scene B, and build gpom-3-B-door-r4 with the timeline page updated in the same round.

Scene D's "You don't. Believing it is your bit." was a callback to the doorstep. None of these drafts has that line any more. Keep D's line as it is (it reads fine on its own), or should one draft plant it?
